title: Scammers use AI to impersonate immigration attorneys to dupe immigrants with fake legal services

reading.body:
Criminals used AI-generated video and image synthesis to impersonate a real immigration attorney on social media platforms, stealing his identity to solicit payments from vulnerable immigrants for fraudulent legal services. The scammers created hundreds of fake profiles across TikTok, Facebook, and Instagram featuring AI-generated likenesses of the attorney, offering services he does not provide and directing victims to make payments through consumer payment apps. The attorney discovered the fraud only when potential clients began calling his office about offers they had seen online.

The deployment failure occurred at the social media platforms where the fake profiles and videos were hosted. These systems did not prevent impersonation at scale or catch the coordinated fraud despite the volume of fake accounts. Detection required manual reporting and removal by a third-party anti-piracy company, which took weeks and removed thousands of profiles after the scheme had already caused financial losses. It is not established whether the platforms' automated systems could have identified the AI-generated content or the pattern of identity theft earlier.

reports.title: Scammers steal identity of renowned Miami attorney to target immigrants on social media
South Florida immigration attorney says AI scammers are using his identity to target immigrants
Scammers use AI to impersonate immigration attorneys to dupe immigrants with fake legal services
Legal resident loses thousands seeking citizenship to AI immigration attorney

summary:
A South Florida immigration attorney with over 30 years of experience says criminals are using artificial intelligence to steal his identity and defraud vulnerable immigrants. Angel Leal reported that scammers have created hundreds of fake videos and social media profiles featuring AI-generated images of him offering immigration services he never provides. One video falsely advertises US residency assistance for undocumented immigrants without deportation orders in exchange for $2,200. Leal discovered the scheme when potential clients started calling his office about these fraudulent offers.

The problem has escalated significantly over the past three months, prompting Leal's firm to hire an anti-piracy company that has successfully removed nearly 6,500 fake profiles across social media platforms, including 3,500 on TikTok, 2,400 on Facebook, and 544 on Instagram. Scammers typically use social media videos directing people to contact numbers via WhatsApp, then send fake contracts and request payment through apps like Venmo, Zelle, or Cash App. Leal is warning immigrants to verify anyone offering legal services online and to avoid anyone requesting immediate payment. He plans to contact local and federal authorities this week to investigate the scams.
